transcript.text: Hi everyone, thanks for being here. As we all know, we want to preserve several of our older relatives' stories in recordings that future family members can listen to, and I'll be coordinating the recording evening since I have the camcorder. We also have the shared family digital drive for storing materials. Before I finalize the plan, I'd like to hear from each of you individually. Nina, could you go first? Please share any preferences, advice, or constraints you have about the recording and file-handling details.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I have an important constraint to share. My grandmother told me she's willing to be recorded only if the interviews stay in the family archive and are not posted publicly online. I haven't had a chance to relay this to you all until now, so I want to make sure it's part of the plan.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Thanks, Nina. I also have something important to share. A friend of mine, Priya, is an audiovisual archivist, and she advised me that for preservation-quality recordings, the audio should be captured as uncompressed WAV files at exactly 48 kHz and 24-bit depth, and that we should make two verified backup copies. I'd like the group to consider incorporating this into the recording and file-handling plan.
transcript.speaker: A3
